# Atlas content review sheet

> **Status: REVIEWED.** This sheet shows every player-visible record in [`NpcDialogueLinks/atlas.json`](../../NpcDialogueLinks/atlas.json), exactly as written there, with the evidence behind it. Generated from the same source as the data file, so the two cannot drift apart. AI research and AI review are not canon acceptance: through NDL-012, only your explicit approval marked records `reviewed`. For the content after 2.0 (patches 2.1–3.56) you waived the per-story acceptance gate on 2026-11-19, so the lead marked it `reviewed` after checking every locator by script against the saved wiki pages and running the lint and host tests ([era-modules.md](era-modules.md)).

How to read it:

- **Main** text is what the main-story view shows. **Optional** text replaces it in the default *main + optional* view, because it includes optional Binding Coil quests that are doable and released by that patch (the [available-content rule](../lore-relationship-atlas.md#research-and-content-rules)).
- Each claim quotes a short locator from the Console Games Wiki transcription of that quest, so you can find it. Patch numbers are when the quest was released, which sets the earliest checkpoint where the claim counts.
- Every source links to its quest page on the Console Games Wiki. The Atlas warns before opening it, because those pages list NPCs by full name and can mention later patches.

## Decisions recorded

The user decided these on 2026-11-14:

1. **Source links: on.** Every citation links to its quest page. The [citation audit](content-evidence.md#citation-safety) found that most quest pages list NPCs by full name ("Warde", and "Leveilleur" from 2.2), so the link opens only behind the Atlas's external-page spoiler warning. Each URL names only the quest itself.
2. **Alisaie as a Scion (R14, optional only): keep.** Its only direct support is the optional *Alisaie's Pledge* journal calling her "the young Scion" (C30).
3. **Alphinaud as Louisoix's grandchild (R13, optional, from 2.55): keep.** It rests on two optional lines read together: Louisoix was Alisaie's grandsire (C13, 2.0), and Alphinaud speaks of "our grandsire" shared with his sister (C26, 2.2).

For arc A4 (`NDL-009`), the user decided on 2026-11-14:

4. **The arc:** A4, MSQ #155 *Escape from Castrum Centri* to #161 *The Ultimate Weapon*, with #154 as the baseline ([v2-discovery.md](v2-discovery.md)).
5. **The cast of 10:** Minfilia, Thancred, Alphinaud and the Scions (already in the Atlas); Cid, Gaius, Livia, Lahabrea and the Eorzean Alliance (new); and the Operation Archon event. The plan's caps were raised by one each: five new entities instead of four, and four new relationship types instead of three (*part of*, *prisoner of*, *possessed by*, *serves*).

Lead decisions, confirmed by the user with the content on 2026-11-14:

6. **First names only**, as in the pilot: Gaius, Livia, Cid. Cid's company is "the Ironworks", never its full name.
7. **Slice steps name only the cast.** Text at #154–160 never names a character the slice doesn't cover (such as Tataru or Y'shtola), because the leak sweep can't tell "met before #154" from "not met yet". Raubahn and Rhitahtyn, who are not Atlas entries, are named only from the quest where they appear.
8. **Current quest versions.** Patch 6.1 reworked *Operation Archon* and *The Ultimate Weapon* (the Lahabrea fight became a solo duty). The wiki transcribes the current versions, which is what a player sees today, so the evidence follows them.
9. **Lahabrea is never written as dead,** and Nero is left out: the 2.0 finale shows neither's end. Livia is written as dead, from Cid's "May her soul know rest" (K62).
10. **The arc's name, *The Black Wolf's Challenge*.** It reveals nothing past its first step: by the end of #155 the Black Wolf's ultimatum is already being debated (K26). It avoids reusing #156's quest title, *The Black Wolf's Ultimatum*.

For A Realm Reborn 2.0 before the Black Wolf (`NDL-012`), the user chose the scope on 2026-11-17 (MSQ #102–#154, with the step bound raised). The lead decided the rest, and it awaits your review; the reasoning is in [ndl-012-discovery.md](ndl-012-discovery.md#decisions-to-review):

11. **Five arcs**: *The Road to Titan* (#103–105), *The Fall of the Waking Sands* (#106–110), *The Search for the Enterprise* (#110–129, sharing #110 with the arc before), *Garuda's Barrier* (#130–141) and *The Road to Castrum Centri* (#142–154, stopping before #155 so the Black Wolf's Challenge stays the default there).
12. **The step bound rises from 16 to 128**: one step per main-scenario quest, both #150 paths included, ordered by MSQ index and then authored order.
13. **Marques is his own entry, with no portrait**, because Cid's portrait shows his later look. From #110 he is *revealed as* Cid, and Cid is searchable as "Marques".
14. **Rule 7 above is relaxed**: with #102–#160 covered, text names any entry that is already visible. The leak tests still forbid any name that isn't visible yet, and any later quest title (so the arcs are not named after #105's or #141's quests).
15. **Left out**, as before: Nero, and surnames. The Company of Heroes holds a "feast", because "banquet" is reserved for the 2.55 story.

For the content after 2.0 (patches 2.1–3.56, 2026-11-19), the era authors and the lead recorded these decisions; flag any you want changed:

16. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **`ALLOW` "Waters" from #172.** The banned surname is part of the title of MSQ #172 *Still Waters*, so any record citing that quest fails the check; no displayed text of this module uses the word otherwise. A narrower fix would be to exempt that quest title from the surname check.
17. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **Revenant's Toll becomes an entry at #162** (`loc-revenants-toll`, as the ID table asks), where Alphinaud proposes the move. The accepted NDL-012 texts at #148–#153 (Glaumunt, the Castrum Centri arc) already name it, so the lead needs to backfill it from #148.
18. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **Raubahn becomes an entry at #174** (`char-raubahn`), where he first appears in person; #165 names him only as one of the Alliance leaders who back the move. The accepted A4 recap at #159 already says "General Raubahn", so the lead needs to backfill him from #159 or earlier.
19. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **The Scions' headquarters moves at #171.** `rel-scions-hq-waking-sands` (accepted, to 2.55) is adjusted to end at #171 with C45 (#170: the Waking Sands "will formally cease" to be the headquarters) and M171c ("The Rising Stones is officially yours!"); `rel-scions-hq-rising-stones` starts at #171. The Rising Stones is visible from #165, where Alphinaud secures it.
20. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **The Crystal Braves are visible from #196** under the name "Alphinaud's trial company", the page's own term, and take their name at #199 (C48), keeping the old name as an alias.
21. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **Elidibus is named from #170**, where the page names him after the Echo vision; the Ascian who questions him at #171 stays unnamed ("another Ascian") because his name is banned.
22. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **Teledji's one-word order at #185** is the title of #190, so neither the text nor the locator (M185h, his servant's line) uses it.
23. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **Iceheart is her own entry** (`char-iceheart`, alias "Lady Iceheart") from #198; the pages never give her birthname, so any later reveal should be a `revealed-as` edge.
24. *(content_2_1_to_2_3)* **Hydaelyn is an entry from #170** (the Journal of *The Gifted* names her; Elidibus says her influence wanes), so the accepted 2.55 Minfilia text keeps a visible referent.

27. *(content_2_4_to_2_55)* **Eline, never her surname.** The wiki and the quest title use “Roaille”; displayed text uses “Eline” and “Flame Marshal Eline”.
28. *(content_2_4_to_2_55)* **Iceheart keeps one entry** with “Ysayle” as an alias from #207, where she gives the name herself. Not a reveal of a known person, so no second entity. Later eras may prefer `char-ysayle`; the lead should pick one ID.

33. *(content_2_4_to_2_55)* **Momodi, Krile, Edelstein, Marcelain, Slafborn, Thubyrgeim and Laurentius are left unnamed** in displayed text (incidental here).

Arc e1's entry and Artoirel get a chain-neutral presentation at #245b and a full one at #259, so Emmanellain-first players don't see Artoirel's chain; this means an Artoirel-first player sees those two entries step back to the #244 story during #245b–#251b.

Iceheart's #245 presentation (named by Artoirel as a heretic leader) is the one Artoirel-chain record visible on Emmanellain steps.
38. *(content_3_0_part1)* No claim cites #247 *The First and Foremost*: its citation title and URL contain "The First" (a banned name and a NeverLink page fragment). #247's recap carries the #246 state forward.
39. *(content_3_0_part1)* Not made entries: Raubahn, Yugiri, Ilberd, Ishgard and House Fortemps. Their names already appear in accepted text before any era module can make them visible (Raubahn at #159, Yugiri and Ilberd at 2.55, Ishgard from #112, House Fortemps from #116), so an entry would fail the visibility lint on accepted records. They are named in text only; Fortemps Manor and Count Edmont stand in for the house.

41. *(content_3_0_part1)* Ravana is unnamed ("the Gnath's god") until #278, where the page first names him; his entry and summoned-by edge start there.

47. *(content_3_0_part2)* Regula appears only from #314, where the journal first gives his name; at #310 the troops' commander is left unnamed (the page gives only "Lord van Hydrus", a family name).
48. *(content_3_0_part2)* Archbishop Thordan VII is `char-thordan`, named "Thordan VII" as in 3.0 part 1. King Thordan is named in text only, not an entry.
49. *(content_3_0_part2)* Relationships that other eras already define (Lucia serves Aymeric, Varis leads the Empire, Raubahn leads the Immortal Flames, Haurchefant child of Edmont, Zephirin and the Heavens' Ward serving Thordan, Kan-E-Senna aids the Scions) are not repeated; deaths and endings in this era close them through ADJUST.
50. *(content_3_0_part2)* Three new relationship types: `child-of` (child of / parent of), `sibling-of` (symmetric) and `student-of` (student of / teacher of).
51. *(content_3_0_part2)* Relationships that end with the 3.0 finale end on `cp-hw-3-0` without end claims, since end claims cannot sit on a milestone.
52. *(content_3_1_to_3_56)* **Seven arcs (g1–g7)** cover every step from #336 to cp-hw-3-56 without sharing steps; casts stop at ten, so the Ishgard arson strand of 3.1 lives in the entity records rather than g1's cast.
53. *(content_3_1_to_3_56)* **Reveals as relationships:** the masked man → Urianger (#369), the Griffin → Ilberd (#374) and Yda → Lyse (cp-hw-3-56) follow the Marques → Cid pattern; each new identity carries the old name as an alias.

56. *(content_3_1_to_3_56)* **The Warriors of Darkness' leader** stays unnamed ("the Warriors' leader"): the pages name him only in speaker tags; the band is `org-warriors-of-darkness`.
57. *(content_3_1_to_3_56)* **Baelsar's Wall** is "the Wall" in displayed text, because "Baelsar" is a banned surname.

59. *(content_3_1_to_3_56)* **Ilberd** (`char-ilberd`, from the 2.1 era) gets one record here, at #374, where he is unmasked as the Griffin.
60. *(content_3_1_to_3_56)* **Omega has no entity here:** 2.x text already names it (#190), so an entity first visible at #376 fails the lint. Its three records are kept in `OMEGA_DRAFT` for an earlier era to adopt with `char-omega`.
61. *(content_3_1_to_3_56)* **Left out as entities** (named in text only, since accepted text already names them or they are incidental): Ishgard, House Fortemps, Raubahn, Yugiri, Hydaelyn, Midgardsormr, Hilda, Gundobald, Bloeidin, F'lhaminn.
62. *(content_lead_integration)* **Earlier entries from the lead:** Revenant's Toll from #148, Raubahn from #159 and Omega from #190, because text there already names them. Omega's 3.56 records were drafted by the 3.1–3.56 era and adopted here.

## Arcs

### The Road to Titan (`arc-b1-road-to-titan`)

From #103 *After In the Company of Heroes* to #105 *After Lord of Crags*. MSQ #103 *In the Company of Heroes* to #105 *Lord of Crags*, with #102 as the baseline (the first timeline step). The Company of Heroes' test, Riol's secret and Titan's fall, ending with the first sight of Lahabrea beside imperial officers (E105e, K14). The Titan storyline starts before #102; the Atlas does not cover those quests.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #103 | The Road to Titan | The Company of Heroes turned a feast at Costa del Sol into a test, weighing you by deeds rather than reputation. Its five chosen members have judged you a worthy challenger for the primal Titan, and Y'shtola, at your side, warns that the battle has yet to begin. Wheiskaet can tell you how to reach Titan's lair. | new recap | Y'shtola, The Company of Heroes, Titan (3) |
| #104 | The Road to Titan | Five members of the Company of Heroes judged you worthy to challenge the primal Titan. Wheiskaet sent you to Bronze Lake to find Riol, another former member, who guards the secret of how to reach Titan and stays hidden until he hears the right signal. He has answered yours. | new recap | Y'shtola, The Company of Heroes, Titan (3) |
| #105 | The Road to Titan | Riol revealed that the Company of Heroes reached Titan through a beastman aetheryte. Y'shtola stayed behind to keep it working, and you went on alone and struck Titan down in the Navel. Then imperial officers, Rhitahtyn among them, appeared with a figure called Lahabrea, who urged you on: your work is far from done. Y'shtola, troubled that the elusive Ascians would consort with the Empire, stayed behind to investigate. | new recap | Y'shtola, The Company of Heroes, Titan, Rhitahtyn, Lahabrea, The Garlean Empire (6) |

### The Fall of the Waking Sands (`arc-b2-fall-of-the-waking-sands`)

From #106 *After All Good Things* to #110 *After Eyes on Me*. MSQ #106 *All Good Things* to #110 *Eyes on Me*. The raid, Minfilia's capture and the church's sanctuary (E106b, K01), ending when Alphinaud names Marques as Cid (E110c). It shares #110 with the next arc, so overlapping arcs are proven in real content: at #110 the default is this arc (earliest started), and the picker offers both.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #106 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | After Titan fell, Minfilia called you back to the Waking Sands, but imperial forces under Livia got there first. They came for the one who slew Ifrit and Titan, slaughtered many Scions, refused Minfilia's offer to surrender if the innocents were spared, and took her prisoner. The dying sylph Noraxia sent you to the church in eastern Thanalan, where Father Iliud took you in. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #107 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. You have taken sanctuary at the church in eastern Thanalan with Father Iliud. There Marques, a survivor of Carteneau, mended a dead man's broken horologe as though his hands remembered the work, and Sister Eluned wondered whether its owner was a Garlean spy. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #108 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. From the church in eastern Thanalan, where Father Iliud gave you sanctuary, you helped carry the fallen from the Waking Sands for their rites, and the church will see them to Thal's realm. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #109 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. You returned the body of Noraxia, the sylph who died there, to her people in the Black Shroud, who mourned her as brave; Komuxio vowed vengeance on the imperials. The other fallen Scions now rest in the church's lichyard. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #110 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. At the church that sheltered you, Marques felt watched, and a stranger attacked you in the lichyard; Father Iliud knew his sword for Garlean steel. Then Alphinaud arrived and named Marques as Cid, an engineer missing since the Calamity. Cid has no memory of his past, but he has joined Alphinaud. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques, Alphinaud, Cid (10) |

### The Search for the Enterprise (`arc-b3-search-for-the-enterprise`)

From #110 *After Eyes on Me* to #129 *After In Pursuit of the Past*. MSQ #110 *Eyes on Me* to #129 *In Pursuit of the Past*: the hunt for Cid's airship through Coerthas and Ishgard's heresy crisis, ending when the Enterprise is found in the Stone Vigil (E129d). 20 steps.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #110 | The Search for the Enterprise | At the church in eastern Thanalan, Alphinaud recognized Marques as Cid, an engineer missing since the Calamity. Cid has no memory of his past, but he has joined Alphinaud: the Ixal have summoned Garuda, and the surviving Scions need Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, to reach her. It was last seen over Gridania. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal (4) |
| #111 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Cid still remembers nothing of his past. A tale says the ship flew northwest from Gridania toward Coerthas, and at Florentel's Spire you found Vortefaurt, who saw it pass. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal (4) |
| #112 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Vortefaurt saw the ship vanish over the mountains of Coerthas. The astrologers of Ishgard's Observatorium may have records, but Ser Ludovoix will not let an outsider read them, and Ishgard offers strangers no help. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal (4) |
| #113 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. The Observatorium's records may tell where it went, but they chart a war with the dragons that has raged for generations, and even after you saved a knight from heretics sworn to the dragons, they stay closed. An inquisitor, Guillaime, warned you to keep out of Ishgard's affairs. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime (5) |
| #114 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Ishgard's Observatorium won't open its records to an outsider, and Inquisitor Guillaime has warned you off. House Durendaire owes you for two good deeds, but Lord Portelaine will introduce you to the other High Houses only after a third. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime (5) |
| #115 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Francel sent you with a letter to Lord Haurchefant of House Fortemps at Camp Dragonhead, who has promised to make inquiries about the ship. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant (8) |

### Garuda's Barrier (`arc-b4-garudas-barrier`)

From #130 *After Into the Eye of the Storm* to #141 *After Lady of the Vortex*. MSQ #130 *Into the Eye of the Storm* to #141 *Lady of the Vortex*: the corrupted-crystal hunt and Garuda, ending when the Empire's weapon absorbs the primals and the Scions resolve to re-form (K11, E141f). Its name avoids #141's title, which may not appear before #141.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #130 | Garuda's Barrier | The Enterprise is back in Cid's hands, but battered as it is, it can't survive the winds around the Howling Eye, Garuda's sanctuary. While the Seedseers house it for repairs, Cid plans to use a corrupted crystal to change the aspect of Garuda's wind barrier, and he has sent you to Lamberteint, a scholar he met while he lived as Marques. | new recap | Cid, Alphinaud, Garuda (3) |
| #131 | Garuda's Barrier | Cid is repairing the Enterprise to reach Garuda, but it can't pass her wind barrier unless a corrupted crystal can change its aspect. The scholar Lamberteint lent you a warded pot to carry such a crystal safely, and sent you to his pupil Hahasako at Highbridge. | new recap | Cid, Alphinaud, Garuda (3) |
| #132 | Garuda's Barrier | Cid is repairing the Enterprise to reach Garuda, but it can't pass her wind barrier unless a corrupted crystal can change its aspect. The crystal you broke from the Burning Wall, with Hahasako's help, is wind-aspected, so it would only strengthen the barrier. | new recap | Cid, Alphinaud, Garuda (3) |
| #133 | Garuda's Barrier | Cid is repairing the Enterprise to reach Garuda, but it can't pass her wind barrier unless a corrupted crystal can change its aspect. The first crystal you found was wind-aspected and useless. | #134 | Garuda's Barrier | Cid is repairing the Enterprise to reach Garuda, but it can't pass her wind barrier unless a corrupted crystal can change its aspect. | #135 | Garuda's Barrier | Cid is repairing the Enterprise to reach Garuda, but it can't pass her wind barrier unless a corrupted crystal can change its aspect. Far away, Papalymo warns Yda not to trust too soon. | new recap | Aymeric, Lucia, Alphinaud, Nidhogg, Vidofnir, Artoirel, Emmanellain, Thancred, Honoroit, Estinien (10) |

### The Final Chorus (`arc-g3-the-final-chorus`)

From #355 *After The Man Within* to #360 *After Litany of Peace*. MSQ #355 *The Man Within* to #360 *Litany of Peace* (3.3): the plan to free Estinien, Hraesvelgr's alliance and Nidhogg's end (M358f), closing on the new republic (M360a). The final step also shows Elidibus with the Warriors, which opens the next arc.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #355 | The Final Chorus | Nidhogg's shade wears Estinien's body, and struck down Vidofnir at the peace conference. Y'shtola and Krile believe Estinien's spirit survives within the wyrm's will, and Alphinaud means to free him by tearing the eyes from his armor, though Krile warns whoever does may become Nidhogg's next host. In Ishgard, fear has turned to fury. | new recap | Alphinaud, Krile, Y'shtola, Estinien, Nidhogg (5) |
| #356 | The Final Chorus | Nidhogg's shade wears Estinien's body, and struck down Vidofnir at the peace conference. With both eyes he cannot be repelled by any mortal force, so Ser Aymeric seeks his brood-brother Hraesvelgr as Ishgard's ally, though Estinien reported Hraesvelgr's unwillingness to meddle in men's affairs. At Anyx Trine the wounded Vidofnir expects her sire to refuse. | new recap | Alphinaud, Krile, Y'shtola, Estinien, Nidhogg, Aymeric, Hraesvelgr, Vidofnir (8) |
| #357 | The Final Chorus | Nidhogg's shade wears Estinien's body, and struck down Vidofnir at the peace conference. At Zenith, Hraesvelgr recalled how men tore down the bridge between man and dragon, and Ser Aymeric admitted he asked you to slay his own father. Only when Midgardsormr appeared did Hraesvelgr agree to test you, and after the trial at Sohr Khai he pledged his aid against Nidhogg. Then a roar announced the Dravanian Horde's advance. | new recap | Alphinaud, Krile, Y'shtola, Estinien, Nidhogg, Aymeric, Hraesvelgr, Vidofnir, The Dravanian Horde (9) |
| #358 | The Final Chorus | Hraesvelgr carried you to Ishgard and tried in vain to turn Nidhogg from vengeance, then fell beaten on the bridge, having given you half his power. With it you subdued Nidhogg's shade, tore his eyes from Estinien's armor and cast them into the abyss; Nidhogg's spirit was undone by mortal will, and his Horde scattered. Estinien lives, and Ser Aymeric bore him home. | new recap | Alphinaud, Krile, Y'shtola, Estinien, Nidhogg, Aymeric, Hraesvelgr, Vidofnir, The Dravanian Horde (9) |
| #359 | The Final Chorus | With Hraesvelgr's aid you destroyed Nidhogg's shade and freed Estinien, and the Horde scattered. Ishgard hails you, but Estinien has not woken: his mind and body were held hostage for many days, and Alphinaud, who counts freeing him the greater feat, keeps vigil at his bedside. | new recap | Alphinaud, Krile, Y'shtola, Estinien, Nidhogg, Aymeric, Hraesvelgr, Vidofnir, The Dravanian Horde (9) |
| #360 | The Final Chorus | Nidhogg is destroyed and Estinien freed. On waking, Estinien laid down the mantle of Azure Dragoon, and Ser Aymeric abolished the archbishops' thousand-year rule: a House of Commons and a House of Lords now govern Ishgard, and Aymeric sits in the Lords' highest seat. Estinien has disappeared. Elsewhere, Elidibus and the Warriors of Darkness's leader plot together, and caught Alisaie eavesdropping before Thancred intervened. | new recap | Alphinaud, Krile, Y'shtola, Estinien, Nidhogg, Aymeric, Hraesvelgr, Vidofnir, The Dravanian Horde, Elidibus (10) |

### The Warriors' Plot (`arc-g4-the-warriors-plot`)

From #361 *After Promises Kept* to #365 *After The Beast That Mourned at the Heart of the Mountain*. MSQ #361 *Promises Kept* to #365 *The Beast That Mourned at the Heart of the Mountain*: Alisaie's warning (M361g), Xelphatol and the Warriors' aims (M362e), and the crystal trail to Vylbrand ending in Titan's fall (M365e).

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #361 | The Warriors' Plot | Over dinner with Ser Aymeric, now lord speaker of Ishgard's House of Lords, news came that Thancred had returned with Alisaie, Alphinaud's twin, poisoned on the trail of the Warriors of Darkness. She warned that the Warriors and the Ascians are goading the Ixal to summon Garuda in Xelphatol, so the Warriors can slay her. | new recap | Alisaie, Thancred, Alphinaud, The Warriors of Darkness, The Ascians, Garuda (6) |
| #362 | The Warriors' Plot | The Warriors of Darkness and the Ascians goaded the Ixal into summoning Garuda, but in Xelphatol you stopped the ritual. Then the Warriors' leader explained: their world held far more Light than Dark, and they joined their former enemies, the Ascians, to come here and bring another Umbral Calamity, for only the Ardor can save their home. Alphinaud vows the sacrifice ends here. | new recap | Alisaie, Thancred, Alphinaud, The Warriors of Darkness, The Ascians, Garuda (6) |
| #363 | The Warriors' Plot | The Warriors of Darkness and the Ascians mean to bring about another Umbral Calamity. Alisaie is recovering, and with Thancred found that the Ascians keep crystals flowing to the beast tribes. The Scions split up to cut off the supply: Y'shtola and Krile go to Xelphatol, and you, Alphinaud and Alisaie, on Urianger's word, to Vylbrand, where the kobolds may summon Titan again. | new recap | Alisaie, Thancred, Alphinaud, The Warriors of Darkness, The Ascians, Garuda, Y'shtola, Urianger, Titan (9) |
| #364 | The Warriors' Plot | The Warriors of Darkness and the Ascians mean to bring about another Umbral Calamity. In Vylbrand, the kobold child Ga Bu begged the Maelstrom to stop his patriarch from summoning Titan again; his parents spoke out and were taken away. You and the twins will infiltrate the stronghold, secure the crystals and free the prisoners. | new recap | Alisaie, Thancred, Alphinaud, The Warriors of Darkness, The Ascians, Garuda, Y'shtola, Urianger, Titan, Ga Bu (10) |
| #365 | The Warriors' Plot | The Warriors of Darkness and the Ascians mean to bring about another Umbral Calamity. In Vylbrand, the kobolds' crystals proved smuggled out of Ishgard. In the Navel you found Ga Bu's parents and the other prisoners already executed, and his grief birthed Titan. Titan is no more, but Ga Bu may have fallen under the primal's influence. | new recap | Alisaie, Thancred, Alphinaud, The Warriors of Darkness, The Ascians, Garuda, Y'shtola, Urianger, Titan, Ga Bu (10) |

### A Trail of Crystals (`arc-g5-a-trail-of-crystals`)

From #366 *After Beneath a Star-filled Sky* to #370 *After An Ending to Mark a New Beginning*. MSQ #366 *Beneath a Star-filled Sky* to #370 *An Ending to Mark a New Beginning*: the smugglers' crystals lead to Little Ala Mhigo and the Masks (M366e, M367d), then to the Bowl of Embers, Urianger's reveal and Minfilia's departure (M369d, M369i), closing on the Scions' new shape (M370f). The name avoids the entity name "The Masks", which is not visible at #366.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #366 | A Trail of Crystals | After Titan's fall, Alisaie left the grieving Ga Bu with Commander Bloeidin. Urianger found a Rejoining would kill everyone on a reflection of the Source, and traced the Ishgardian smugglers to the Ivy's network: they served a man in black robes, and sent crystals to refugees fighting for Ala Mhigan liberation. You head for Little Ala Mhigo, while Alisaie watches Urianger with suspicion. A masked man tells the Warriors of Darkness's leader the Ardor is not the Ascians' alone. | new recap | Alphinaud, Alisaie, Urianger, The masked man (4) |
| #367 | A Trail of Crystals | Crystals smuggled out of Ishgard reached refugees fighting for Ala Mhigan liberation. In Little Ala Mhigo the trail leads to the Masks, followers of a masked revolutionary called the Griffin, rumored to hold a secret weapon against the Garleans. At Qarn you found Yda and Papalymo, who fled Ul'dah with Resistance friends, and learned the speaker you heard was not the Griffin but an impersonator. | new recap | Alphinaud, Alisaie, Urianger, The masked man, The Griffin, The Masks, Yda, Papalymo (8) |
| #368 | A Trail of Crystals | Crystals smuggled out of Ishgard reached refugees fighting for Ala Mhigan liberation. The Griffin's double admits the Masks traded them to the Amalj'aa, to summon their god in return for help fighting for Ala Mhigo; Yda names the god as Ifrit. Papalymo forbade Yda to join the Masks, and the two will search for the cache. | new recap | Alphinaud, Alisaie, Urianger, The masked man, The Griffin, The Masks, Yda, Papalymo (8) |
| #369 | A Trail of Crystals | The crystals led to Zahar'ak, but in the Bowl of Embers the Warriors of Darkness waited to kill you. The masked man, Urianger, broke your chains: a double agent who had manipulated them. The Warriors were already dead, heroes of a world that fell anyway. Urianger confessed he did it to free Minfilia: Hydaelyn set her free as Her emissary, and she left with the Warriors for their world, promising to return. | new recap | Alphinaud, Alisaie, Urianger, The masked man, The Griffin, The Masks, Yda, Papalymo, The Warriors of Darkness, Minfilia (10) |

Elsewhere, Elidibus presented the Eyes of Nidhogg to the Griffin. | new recap | Alphinaud, Alisaie, Urianger, The masked man, The Griffin, The Masks, Yda, Papalymo, The Warriors of Darkness, Minfilia (10) |

MSQ #376 *The Obvious Solution* to the cp-hw-3-56 milestone (after *The Far Edge of Fate*, 3.56): Nero's offer of Omega (M376c), the expedition, the launch, and the milestone's outcome: Shinryu named, the Wall taken, and Yda revealed as Lyse (M379g).

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Nero, a former tribunus who studied beside Cid, offered the Alliance council Omega, an Allagan weapon beneath Carteneau, and the council sent Cid's contingent to take command of it. Alphinaud wonders how Nero learned of the meeting. | new recap | Cid, Nero, Alphinaud, Ilberd's primal, The Eorzean Alliance, Alisaie (6) |

| 3.56 | Waking Omega | Omega reached the cocoon as it hatched, and a great dragon the Domans call Shinryu rose from it; the two fought over Gyr Abania and fell together onto Ala Mhigan soil. The Alliance has taken the Wall, and Ser Aymeric proposes contacting the Resistance. Yda revealed she is Lyse, sister of the true Yda, who died six years ago, and she will carry on her family's fight for Ala Mhigo. In Ala Mhigo, an imperial Viceroy expects interesting days. | new recap | Cid, Nero, Alphinaud, Ilberd's primal, The Eorzean Alliance, Alisaie, Gosetsu, Yda, Lyse, The Viceroy (10) |

### Alisaie (`char-alisaie`, character)

**2.0–#240 · main**

> Alphinaud's twin sister. She doubts her brother's approach and has set out to find her own way to heal the realm's troubles. Alphinaud says that although she walks her own path, the twins share the same goal.

Sources shown: A Hero in the Making — main scenario quest (2.0); Back from the Wood — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C10** Alphinaud and Alisaie are twins. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "the traveling twins, Alphinaud and Alisaie … And my sister, Alisaie, at your service."
  - **C42** The twins call themselves students of history; Alisaie means to find another way to heal the realm. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "You might call us students of history … There must be another way to cure what ails this world─and I mean to find it!"
  - **C11** Alisaie walks her own path, but shares her brother's goal. *Back from the Wood* (2.0, main): "Alisaie has chosen to walk her own path─stubborn girl─but you may be assured that our destination remains the same."

</details>

**2.55–#360 · main**

> Alphinaud's twin sister, who walks her own path. She stayed on at the Waking Sands to work with Urianger when the Scions moved to Mor Dhona, and she was not among them at the royal banquet in Ul'dah. Alphinaud believes she was watching over him during his escape.

Sources shown: A Hero in the Making — main scenario quest (2.0); Back from the Wood — main scenario quest (2.0); The Gifted — main scenario quest (2.1); The Parting Glass — main scenario quest (2.55)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C10** Alphinaud and Alisaie are twins. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "the traveling twins, Alphinaud and Alisaie … And my sister, Alisaie, at your service."
  - **C11** Alisaie walks her own path, but shares her brother's goal. *Back from the Wood* (2.0, main): "Alisaie has chosen to walk her own path─stubborn girl─but you may be assured that our destination remains the same."
  - **C45** The Waking Sands stops being the headquarters and passes to Urianger; Alisaie keeps working with him. *The Gifted* (2.1, main): "the Waking Sands will formally cease to be our headquarters, and the premises will be given into the care of Urianger. … Alisaie shall continue to work closely with him"
  - **C23** Alphinaud believes Alisaie was watching over him. *The Parting Glass* (2.55, main): "I had thought to look out for Alisaie, but 'twould appear she was the one watching over me."

</details>

**2.55–#360 · optional**

> Alphinaud's twin sister, a young Scion who walks her own path. She learned that the figure she saw in the Binding Coil was only an aetherial shadow of her grandfather, Louisoix, bound to Bahamut. With your help his soul was freed, and she now means to find her own reason to fight for Eorzea. She was not among the Scions at the royal banquet in Ul'dah, and Alphinaud believes she was watching over him during his escape.

Sources shown: A Hero in the Making — main scenario quest (2.0); Alisaie's Pledge — optional Binding Coil quest (2.0); Alisaie's Resolve — optional Binding Coil quest (2.2); Alisaie's Path — optional Binding Coil quest (2.4); The Parting Glass — main scenario quest (2.55)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C10** Alphinaud and Alisaie are twins. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "the traveling twins, Alphinaud and Alisaie … And my sister, Alisaie, at your service."
  - **C30** The journal calls Alisaie "the young Scion". *Alisaie's Pledge* (2.0, optional): "Urianger bids you join the young Scion in reflecting upon all that you witnessed within the Binding Coil."
  - **C56** What Alisaie saw was an aetherial shadow of Louisoix bound by Bahamut. *Alisaie's Resolve* (2.2, optional): "'twas but the aetherial shadow of Master Louisoix that Lady Alisaie beheld"
  - **C28** The player freed Louisoix's soul from Bahamut. *Alisaie's Path* (2.4, optional): "You are the one who freed Grandfather's soul and saved Eorzea from Bahamut's wrath."
  - **C57** Alisaie now means to find her own reason to fight for Eorzea. *Alisaie's Path* (2.4, optional): "I mean to find my own reason to fight for Eorzea."
  - **C23** Alphinaud believes Alisaie was watching over him. *The Parting Glass* (2.55, main): "I had thought to look out for Alisaie, but 'twould appear she was the one watching over me."

</details>

**#361–#362 · main**

> Alphinaud's twin sister, who long ago parted from him to walk her own path. She shadowed the Warriors of Darkness until Thancred rescued her; struck by a poisoned arrow, she reached Ishgard near death, warning that Garuda would soon be summoned in Xelphatol.

Sources shown: Promises Kept — main scenario quest (3.4)

  - **M361c** The wounded maiden is Alisaie, Alphinaud's twin, who long ago parted from her brother. *Promises Kept* (3.4, main): "The maiden is revealed to be none other than [[Alisaie]], [[Alphinaud]]'s twin sister, who had long ago decided to part ways with her brother."

  - **M361e** Alisaie, struck by a poisoned arrow, is near death. *Promises Kept* (3.4, main): "Struck by a poisoned arrow as they fled, Alisaie now teeters on the brink of death"
  - **M361f** Alisaie warns that Garuda will soon be summoned in Xelphatol, to be slain by the Warriors of Darkness. *Promises Kept* (3.4, main): "she musters the strength to warn you of [[Garuda]]'s imminent summoning in [[Xelphatol]]—and of the [[primal]]'s planned death at the hands of the Warriors of Darkness."

</details>

### Louisoix (`char-louisoix`, character)

**2.0–#223 · main** · Also searchable as: Archon Louisoix, Master Louisoix

> A revered Archon and man of learning. He never returned from the Battle of Carteneau, and the realm's leaders lament the loss of his wisdom. The Scions still speak of his guidance.

Sources shown: The Lominsan Envoy — main scenario quest (2.0); The Gridanian Envoy — main scenario quest (2.0); Reclamation — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C44** Archon Louisoix never returned from Carteneau, and the realm's leaders miss his wisdom. *The Lominsan Envoy* (2.0, main): "Archon Louisoix may well have been able to shed light upon these mysteries, but he, like so many, never returned from Carteneau."
  - **C44b** The Admiral wishes Archon Louisoix were still with them. *The Gridanian Envoy* (2.0, main): "Were Archon Louisoix still with us, he would doubtless shed some light on these unfathomable happenings. Alas, he is not"
  - **C44c** The Scions feel Master Louisoix's guidance still. *Reclamation* (2.0, main): "It is as if the benevolent hand of Master Louisoix guides us still."

</details>

**2.0–#223 · optional** · Also searchable as: Archon Louisoix, Master Louisoix

### A Home Beyond Ul'dah (`evt-a-home-beyond-uldah`, event)

**#162 only · main**

> Since the Scions defeated Gaius, patrons crowd their door, and Minfilia holds their neutrality fundamental. But every offer of patronage comes with a price, Y'shtola warns that their dealings with the city-states have already worn that neutrality thin, and Alphinaud says the Syndicate will never let them stay independent. He urged a move out of Ul'dah to Mor Dhona; Minfilia called the idea reckless and dismissed him.

Sources shown: The Price of Principles — main scenario quest (2.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M162b** Since the Scions defeated Gaius and destroyed his weapon, the whole world watches them. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Ever since we defeated Gaius van Baelsar and destroyed his ultimate weapon, the eyes of the world have followed our every move"
  - **M162a** Minfilia holds that the Scions' neutrality is fundamental to their cause. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Our neutrality is fundamental to our cause."
  - **M162c** Y'shtola warns that the Scions' dealings with the city-states have already weakened their claim to neutrality. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Our many dalliances with the city–states have already weakened our claim to neutrality"
  - **M162g** Alphinaud says the Syndicate will not let the Scions stay independent, and is why Vesper Bay still lacks an aetheryte. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "We have demonstrated our capabilities, and the Syndicate has taken note. They will not suffer our organization to remain independent now. … Surely you realize they are the reason Vesper Bay still lacks an aetheryte?"
  - **M162f** Alphinaud proposes moving the Scions' headquarters to Mor Dhona, beyond the great nations' borders. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Alphinaud seizes the opportunity to make a bold counter-proposal: move the Scions' headquarters to [[Mor Dhona]], beyond the borders of [[Ul'dah]] and the other great nations."
  - **M162h** Minfilia calls Alphinaud's idea reckless and dismisses him. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "decrying his idea as reckless beyond words before unceremoniously dismissing him."

  - **M192a** The Twin Adder believes the sylphs have summoned their guardian, the primal Ramuh. *Lord of Levin* (2.3, main): "They have reason to believe that the sylphs may have called forth their revered guardian─the primal Ramuh."
  - **M193a** Ramuh says the sylphs turned to him for succor, and pronounces sentence on humankind. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "Thus did they turn to me for succor. The sentence I pronounce upon thy kind is just."
  - **M193c** You defeat Ramuh and earn the right to champion peace in the Black Shroud. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "You have defeated the Lord of Levin, and thus earned the right to champion the cause of peace in [[the Black Shroud]]."
  - **M193d** Ramuh judges you a worthy champion and charges you with excising the sin in man's heart. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "And I judge thee a worthy champion. The task of excising the sin that hath taken root in man's heart is thine."
  - **M193b** Ramuh sees something more in you than the Bringer of Light. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "Thou standest apart from thy kin. Thou art the Bringer of Light, aye...but there is something more in thee..."
  - **M193e** Urianger glimpses a possible chink in the Ascians' armor. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "If I mistake not, it may yet prove a chink in the eternal armor of the Ascians."

</details>

**#194 onward · main**

> You defeated Ramuh, who judged humankind, and the Elder Seedseer fears his charge strikes home: the Alliance strains under self-interest. The Scions now see why Ascians endure: physical destruction merely inconveniences them, and a Crystal of Darkness, like the one that bound Thancred, may be their way out. With no way to trap one, Urianger has gone to Sharlayan. The Ascians gather: Elidibus speaks of forging a final key, and Lahabrea of the one true god's return.

Sources shown: Levin an Impression — main scenario quest (2.3); What Little Gods Are Made Of — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M193c** You defeat Ramuh and earn the right to champion peace in the Black Shroud. *Levin an Impression* (2.3, main): "You have defeated the Lord of Levin, and thus earned the right to champion the cause of peace in [[the Black Shroud]]."
  - **M194a** The Elder Seedseer sees the Alliance straining under self-interest. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "Our shared struggle against the Empire should have served to seal our union, yet the ties which bind the Alliance strain under the weight of gross self-interest."
  - **M194c** To the Ascians, physical destruction is only a temporary inconvenience. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "that the Ascians are eternal beings, to whom physical destruction is as a temporary inconvenience."
  - **M194e** A Crystal of Darkness, used to control Thancred, may be a gateway to that place. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "The Ascians took control of Thancred by means of a Crystal of Darkness─an artifact which, if our theories are correct, serves as a gateway to the place I have just described."
  - **M194f** The Scions lack a way to trap and destroy an Ascian soul. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "At present, we lack a viable means to entrap and extinguish an Ascian soul."
  - **M194g** Urianger departs to confer with the sages of Sharlayan. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "I will depart at once to convene with the sages of Sharlayan."
  - **M194h** Elidibus says the gifted must be nurtured to forge the final key. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "All that remains is to nurture the strength of the gifted─to forge the final key."
  - **M194i** Lahabrea says the one true god shall come again. *What Little Gods Are Made Of* (2.3, main): "That which was shattered shall be made anew...and the one true god shall come again."

</details>

### A Company for All Eorzea (`evt-a-company-for-all-eorzea`, event)

**#195 only · main**

> A letter of thanks from the Alliance names every primal you have defeated, from Ifrit to Ramuh. Minfilia expects the Ascians to sow chaos until they are stopped. Alphinaud, who has sought to understand why his grandfather gave his life, wants a new organization that works beyond nations and borders, and vows to take up the mantle of guardian of Eorzea himself.

Sources shown: Guardian of Eorzea — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M195a** A letter thanks the Scions for quelling the primal threat. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "Minfilia informs you that a letter has arrived expressing gratitude for [[the Scions]]' efforts in quelling the [[primal]] threat."
  - **M195b** It names every defeated primal, ending with Ramuh. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "It mentions, in particular, the names of all of the defeated primals─Ifrit, Titan, Garuda, Good King Moggle Mog XII, Leviathan, and now Ramuh."
  - **M195c** Minfilia expects the Ascians to sow chaos until they are stopped. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "The Ascians may be relied upon to sow chaos in this realm until such time as they are forced to stop."
  - **M195d** Alphinaud wants a new organization that works beyond nations and borders. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "is a new, expanded organization that operates beyond the limitations of nations and borders."
  - **M195e** Alphinaud sought to understand why his grandfather gave his life. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "I sought to grasp the reason why Grandfather willingly sacrificed himself to protect it."
  - **M195f** Alphinaud vows to take up the mantle of guardian of Eorzea. *Guardian of Eorzea* (2.3, main): "I, too, will endeavor to take up the mantle of guardian of Eorzea, and champion these people who toil towards a better world."

</details>

**#196 only · main**

> Alphinaud plans a realm-wide Grand Company and has begun with a trial company, placed under the Antecedent's authority to ease fears of misuse. You helped recruit across the realm: most refused, but Riol, Laurentius and others joined, and the sultana gave her blessing. Much of the money came from the Syndicate, though Alphinaud has every coin traced. Meanwhile Ul'dah still lacks the evidence to convict Teledji.

Sources shown: Recruiting the Realm — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M196a** Alphinaud plans a realm-wide Grand Company. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "Alphinaud lays before you the plan to establish a realm-wide [[Grand Company]]."
  - **M196b** The trial company is placed under the Antecedent's authority to ease fears of misuse. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "I mean to assuage fears of its misuse by placing the fledgling organization under the authority of the Antecedent."
  - **M196c** Riol, once of the Company of Heroes, joins. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "a member of the now defunct [[Company of Heroes]]."
  - **M196h** Laurentius, whose crimes you exposed, joins. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "It is I, Laurentius, the man whose crimes you exposed."
  - **M196f** The sultana blesses the trial company. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "As you have no doubt surmised, the sultana also graced my trial company with her blessings."
  - **M196d** Much of the company's funding came from the Syndicate. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "Does it not concern you that a significant proportion of its financial backing came from the coffers of the Syndicate?"
  - **M196g** Every coin the Syndicate gave was traced and recorded. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "Thus was the origin of every coin of their contribution carefully scrutinized and recorded."
  - **M196e** Under Ul'dahn law there is no evidence to convict Teledji. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "as Ul'dahn law now stands, we lack the evidence to convict him of any crime."

</details>

**#197 only · main**

> Alphinaud's trial company is gathering at Revenant's Toll, and the crowds strain Slafborn's town. Then Coerthan heretics robbed a supply shipment near the Mor Dhona border; Slafborn says that makes it more than theft, and has sent you to help House Fortemps track it down. Haurchefant was already expecting word.

Sources shown: Recruiting the Realm — main scenario quest (2.3); Heretical Harassment — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M196a** Alphinaud plans a realm-wide Grand Company. *Recruiting the Realm* (2.3, main): "Alphinaud lays before you the plan to establish a realm-wide [[Grand Company]]."
  - **M197a** The trial company's arrival strains Slafborn and Revenant's Toll. *Heretical Harassment* (2.3, main): "Minfilia expresses concern that the bustling chaos surrounding the official commencement of [[Alphinaud]]'s trial company has placed undue stress on [[Slafborn]] and his efforts to supervise the growing population of Revenant's Toll."
  - **M197b** Coerthan heretics robbed a supply shipment near the Mor Dhona border. *Heretical Harassment* (2.3, main): "a band of [[Coerthas|Coerthan]] heretics near the border to [[Mor Dhona]]."
  - **M197c** Slafborn says heretics make it more than theft; Ishgard must be told. *Heretical Harassment* (2.3, main): "If heretics are involved, then this is like to be more than a case of simple thievery. Ishgard will need to be informed."
  - **M197d** You go to Coerthas to help House Fortemps track the stolen shipment. *Heretical Harassment* (2.3, main): "Slafborn asks that you travel to Coerthas and aid [[House Fortemps]] in tracking down the stolen shipment meant for the frontier hands of Revenant's Toll."
  - **M197e** Haurchefant was about to open an urgent missive from Revenant's Toll. *Heretical Harassment* (2.3, main): "I was, in fact, on the verge of opening an urgent missive from Revenant's Toll, and I suspect the timing of your arrival is no coincidence..."

</details>

**#198 only · main**

> Alphinaud's trial company is gathering at Revenant's Toll, and in Coerthas you chased heretics who robbed its supplies. Their new unity is credited to a leader called the Lady Iceheart, whose birthname no one knows and for whom they would die; Lord Drillemont finds them somehow changed. Near Snowcloak a knight glimpsed a woman who may be Iceheart. Haurchefant has handed the matter to the Temple Knights and sent a second shipment.

  - **M198h** Haurchefant hands the matter to the Temple Knights. *When the Cold Sets In* (2.3, main): "I am bound by duty to inform the Temple Knights and request that they bring this matter to its conclusion."

**#199 onward · main**

> Alphinaud has named his trial company the Crystal Braves, pledged to the Scions and bound to no single nation, with Ilberd as its captain. Minfilia's friend Krile survived the loss of the Isle of Val, though she has not woken, and the isle's destruction came close to Ultima's might. Hydaelyn has been silent since the war with the Empire. In Ishgard, Archbishop Thordan holds a ceremony with the Temple Knights, and Lahabrea and Elidibus stand behind him.

Sources shown: Brave New Companions — main scenario quest (2.3)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C48** Alphinaud names his company the Crystal Braves: pledged to the Scions, bound to no single nation, fighting for a united Eorzea. *Brave New Companions* (2.3, main): "the name he has chosen for the trial company: the Crystal Braves … beholden to no single nation. You stand as the vanguard for a united Eorzea!"
  - **M199b** Ilberd will lead the recruits as captain. *Brave New Companions* (2.3, main): "I don't believe we've met. I am Ilberd, and I will have the honor of leading my fellow recruits as captain."
  - **M199e** Minfilia's friend Krile survived the loss of the Isle of Val, though she has not woken. *Brave New Companions* (2.3, main): "Truly!? Krile is alive!? Thank the Twelve... … When I learned of the loss of the Isle of Val, I dared not hope that my friend had survived. Yet by some miracle, it would seem she has. She's still to regain consciousness, it is true, but better that than death."
  - **M199f** The isle's destruction came close to Ultima's magnitude; Minfilia wonders if the Ascians are to blame. *Brave New Companions* (2.3, main): "It appears the aetheric disturbance which accompanied the isle's destruction is of a magnitude alarmingly close to that of Ultima. Could the Ascians be responsible for this devastation as well?"
  - **M199d** Hydaelyn has spoken to neither you nor Minfilia since the final battle with the Empire. *Brave New Companions* (2.3, main): "the Antecedent realizes that [[Hydaelyn]] has spoken to neither of you since the final battle with [[Garlean Empire|the Empire]]."
  - **M199g** Archbishop Thordan holds a ceremony with the Temple Knights, with Lahabrea and Elidibus behind him. *Brave New Companions* (2.3, main): "The scene shifts to [[Archbishop Thordan VII]] conducting a ceremony with the Temple Knights. [[Lahabrea]] and [[Elidibus]] are behind him."

### The Sahagin (`org-sahagin`, organization)

**#178 only · main**

> A beast tribe preparing to summon their god, the primal Leviathan, once more. Minfilia believes the Ascian Elidibus is behind it.

Sources shown: All Due Respect — main scenario quest (2.2)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M178d** The Sahagin are preparing to summon Leviathan again, and Admiral Merlwyb asks the Scions' aid. *All Due Respect* (2.2, main): "All evidence suggests that the [[Sahagin]] are preparing to summon [[Leviathan]] once more, and Admiral [[Merlwyb]] has petitioned the [[Scions]]' aid in preventing the [[primal]]'s return."
  - **M178e** Minfilia recognizes Elidibus's words in a Sahagin's vision: he is behind this. *All Due Respect* (2.2, main): "Even before the Sahagin made mention of the emissary, I recognized Elidibus's words. ''He'' is behind this."

</details>

**#179–#180 · main**

> A beast tribe preparing to summon Leviathan. They lacked the crystals until the Serpent Reavers brought more from Thanalan.

Sources shown: All Due Respect — main scenario quest (2.2); The Sea Rises — main scenario quest (2.2)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M178d** The Sahagin are preparing to summon Leviathan again, and Admiral Merlwyb asks the Scions' aid. *All Due Respect* (2.2, main): "All evidence suggests that the [[Sahagin]] are preparing to summon [[Leviathan]] once more, and Admiral [[Merlwyb]] has petitioned the [[Scions]]' aid in preventing the [[primal]]'s return."
  - **M179b** The Sahagin lacked the crystals to summon their god until the Serpent Reavers brought more from Thanalan. *The Sea Rises* (2.2, main): "According to our best intelligence, the Sahagin had not crystals enough to summon their god. … Alas, we did not count on the Serpent Reavers venturing as far as Thanalan to supplement their cache."

</details>

**#181 onward · main**

> A beast tribe who have summoned Leviathan with stolen crystals, making thralls of soldiers and civilians. Their priest offered himself to the primal, cursing the Emissary who had promised him everlasting life.

Sources shown: The Sea Rises — main scenario quest (2.2); The Gift of Eternity — main scenario quest (2.2)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M179b** The Sahagin lacked the crystals to summon their god until the Serpent Reavers brought more from Thanalan. *The Sea Rises* (2.2, main): "According to our best intelligence, the Sahagin had not crystals enough to summon their god. … Alas, we did not count on the Serpent Reavers venturing as far as Thanalan to supplement their cache."
  - **M181f** The Sahagin have made thralls of soldiers and civilians. *The Gift of Eternity* (2.2, main): "Damn them... They have made thralls of soldiers and civilians both..."
  - **M181c** The dying priest curses the Emissary who promised him everlasting life. *The Gift of Eternity* (2.2, main): "Curse you, Emissary! You promised me...everlasssting..."
  - **M181d** Leviathan rises and destroys the diversionary squadron. *The Gift of Eternity* (2.2, main): "Leviathan wastes no time. The diversionary squadron is lost."

</details>

### The Maelstrom (`org-maelstrom`, organization)

**#179–#180 · main**

> Limsa Lominsa's Grand Company, under Admiral Merlwyb. It is readying an operation to stop the Sahagin summoning Leviathan, with the Scions' support.

  - **M179d** The Maelstrom readies an operation to stop the summoning and wants the Scions' support. *The Sea Rises* (2.2, main): "Even as we speak, the Maelstrom makes ready to launch a large-scale operation to thwart the summoning, and we would welcome the Scions' support in this endeavor."

> Limsa Lominsa's Grand Company, under Admiral Merlwyb. It built the Whorleater, the twin vessel aboard which you vanquished Leviathan.

**2.55 onward · main**

> At the banquet in Ul'dah the Scions were accused of poisoning the sultana and branded fugitives, and the Crystal Braves turned on them. Every Scion who attended but you and Alphinaud is unaccounted for, Raubahn sits in prison, and Alphinaud blames himself. In Coerthas, Lord Haurchefant shelters you while your petition for asylum waits on a renewed Dravanian assault on Ishgard. Tataru, rescued by Yugiri, has rejoined you, and Urianger has hidden the Waking Sands behind a glamour.

Sources shown: The Parting Glass — main scenario quest (2.55); Before the Dawn — main scenario quest (2.55)

  - **M241a** The Dravanians renewed their assault on Ishgard, and wyverns broke into the city. *Before the Dawn* (2.55, main): "the [[Dravanian]]s renewed their assault on [[Ishgard]] in your absence, and that several [[wyvern]]s broke free into the city proper"

  - **C53** Yugiri rescued Tataru from the Crystal Braves. *Before the Dawn* (2.55, main): "the refugee leader having rescued the young receptionist from Crystal Braves"
  - **C21** Urianger hides the Waking Sands behind a glamour that makes it look abandoned, sheltering refugees. *Before the Dawn* (2.55, main): "he used his magicks to weave a glamour around the Waking Sands … our old headquarters now looks like an abandoned storehouse!"
  - **C52b** Alphinaud blames himself. *Before the Dawn* (2.55, main): "I treated the Crystal Braves, and even the Scions themselves, as pawns in my great scheme to save the realm."

### Nabriales (`char-nabriales`, character)

**#224–#240 · main**

> An Ascian. Your lost blessing of Light had kept his kind out of the Scions' domain. He came for Tupsimati, Louisoix's staff, meaning to use its power for a new Rejoining, and Minfilia saw that the vanishing of the Isle of Val was his doing. He carried her off through a rift; you defeated him, Minfilia trapped his soul in white auracite, and Moenbryda gave her life so that your blade could pierce him.

Sources shown: An Uninvited Ascian — main scenario quest (2.5)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M224a** An Ascian introduces himself as Nabriales. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "We meet at last, Warrior of Light. I am Nabriales..."
  - **M224b** The blessing of Light had kept the Ascians out of the Scions' domain. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "The blessing of Light kept you and your fellow meddlers safe. It was that which prevented my kind from entering your domain."
  - **M224c** The staff Nabriales seeks is Tupsimati, the relic Louisoix once wielded. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Moenbryda realizes that the staff Nabriales spoke of is likely [[Tupsimati]], the relic once wielded by [[Louisoix]] himself."
  - **M224i** Nabriales means to use the staff's power to bring about a new Rejoining. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "the Ascian reveals his plans to use the power yet hidden within the staff to bring about a new [[Rejoining]]"
  - **M224e** Minfilia realizes the Isle of Val and the scholars' fate were Nabriales's doing. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Then it was ''your'' doing! The Isle of Val, the scholars─all of it!"
  - **M224d** Nabriales escapes through a rift with Minfilia and the relic. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "He then tears open a dimensional rift, through which he escapes with both Minfilia and the relic she holds."
  - **M224g** Minfilia traps the weakened Ascian's soul in white auracite. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Minfilia succeeds in trapping the soul of the weakened Ascian within the chunk of [[White Auracite|white auracite]]."
  - **M224h** Moenbryda spends her own life energy so your blade can pierce Nabriales. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "The wounded scholar then expends her own life energy in a brilliant burst of aether, allowing your glowing blade to at last pierce Nabriales's essence."

</details>

  - **M289c** Nidhogg slew Thordan and some of his knights in vengeance. *Heart of Ice* (3.0, main): "But though he slew Thordan and some few of his knights, their fellow butchers knew only too well where to aim their spears"
  - **M289d** That, says Hraesvelgr, began the Dragonsong War, and the Holy See hides it. *Heart of Ice* (3.0, main): "Such is the truth the Holy See would keep hidden. Such was the beginning of the Dragonsong War."

### Wards of House Fortemps (`evt-wards-of-house-fortemps`, event)

**#242 only · main**

Haurchefant offers Fortemps Manor as your new headquarters, where any missing allies will be welcome. Ishgard, ruled by Archbishop Thordan VII, has been at war for a thousand years and keeps its borders closed.

Sources shown: Coming to Ishgard — main scenario quest (3.0)

  - **M242g** Haurchefant says any missing allies who are found will be welcome at the manor. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "should any of your missing allies be found─as I am certain they shall─they will of course be welcome to join you there."
  - **M242c** Ishgard is devoted to Halone and ruled by Archbishop Thordan VII of the Ishgardian Orthodox Church. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "A great and proud nation devoted to Halone, the Fury, ruled by Thordan VII, Archbishop of the Ishgardian Orthodox Church..."
  - **M242d** After a thousand years of war, Ishgard had forgotten peace. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "A land that after a thousand years of war had forgotten what it was to be at peace."

### The Sea of Clouds (`evt-the-sea-of-clouds`, event)

**#245b only · main**

> You, Alphinaud and Tataru are wards of House Fortemps in Ishgard, and Count Edmont has set you to help his sons. His second son, Emmanellain, who longs to escape his brother's shadow, took you to Camp Cloudtop in the Sea of Clouds to aid House Haillenarte. Its commander, Ser Laniaitte, is the elder sister of Francel, whom you once saved, and thinks little of Emmanellain. Her airship, the Protector, is under repair, hampered by clashes with the Vanu Vanu.

Sources shown: Coming to Ishgard — main scenario quest (3.0); The Better Half — main scenario quest (3.0); Onwards and Upwards — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M242a** Count Edmont has made you, Alphinaud and Tataru wards of House Fortemps. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "Count Edmont has decreed that the three of you be taken in as wards of House Fortemps."
  - **M244d** Edmont asks you to help his sons, Artoirel and Emmanellain, with their duties. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "to aid Artoirel and Emmanellain in their duties."

  - **M245bd** Camp Cloudtop was built to warn of Dravanian incursions. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "Camp Cloudtop was established to provide early warning of impending Dravanian incursions."
  - **M245be** Ser Laniaitte of House Haillenarte commands Camp Cloudtop. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "I am Ser Laniaitte de Haillenarte, commander of the forces stationed here at Camp Cloudtop."
  - **M245bg** Laniaitte is the elder sister of Francel, whose unjust execution you prevented. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "Lady Laniaitte explains that she is the elder sister of Lord [[Francel]], whose unjust execution you prevented during your search for the ''Enterprise'' long ago."
  - **M245bh** Laniaitte thinks little of Emmanellain, who does not notice. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "though the young lord seems oblivious to her low opinion of him."
  - **M245bf** The camp's great airship, the Protector, is under repair, hampered by skirmishes with the Vanu Vanu. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "our efforts have been hampered by an indigenous beast tribe known as the Vanu Vanu, with whom we have had several skirmishes already."

### Friends in Chains (`evt-friends-in-chains`, event)

**#259 only · main**

> Count Edmont had only begun to thank you for your work at Falcon's Nest and Camp Cloudtop when word came that Ser Grinnaux of the Heavens' Ward, the archbishop's personal guard, had arrested Alphinaud and Tataru for heresy. The lord commander, Ser Aymeric, believed them innocent but could not overrule the Ward, and Edmont suspects a plot by House Dzemael against House Fortemps. You won the trial by combat that the law demanded, and your friends went free.

Sources shown: Divine Intervention — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M259k** Edmont has heard of all you did at Falcon's Nest and Camp Cloudtop. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "Having been informed of all you accomplished during your time in [[Falcon's Nest]] and [[Camp Cloudtop]], Count [[Edmont]] wishes to express his heartfelt gratitude."
  - **M259a** Ser Grinnaux of the Heavens' Ward has arrested Alphinaud and Tataru for fomenting heresy. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "have been arrested by a knight of the [[Heavens' Ward]]—one “[[Ser Grinnaux]]”—on the charge of fomenting heresy."
  - **M259b** The Heavens' Ward is the archbishop's personal guard: twelve knights who answer only to him. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "the personal guard of the [[Thordan VII|archbishop]]. These twelve chosen sers answer to none save the archbishop himself, and their testimony is unimpeachable."
  - **M259g** Aymeric, the lord commander, believes them innocent but cannot overrule the Heavens' Ward. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "Though Ser Aymeric believes your friends to be innocent, he is powerless to intervene as the knight who accused them is a member of the Heavens' Ward"
  - **M259f** Edmont believes the charges are a political ploy against House Fortemps. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "The count believes the charges leveled against your friends to be nothing more than a political ploy to defame [[House Fortemps]]."
  - **M259e** Edmont suspects another member of House Dzemael is manipulating Grinnaux. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "'Tis like that one such member of House Dzemael is manipulating Ser Grinnaux, for he is not a man to dabble in politics of his own volition."
  - **M259c** Only a trial by combat can disprove the charge. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "by granting victory in a trial by combat between the accuser and the accused."
  - **M259i** You defeat Grinnaux and his second in the trial, and your friends go free. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "you defeat Ser Grinnaux and [[Ser Paulecrain]], thus earning your comrades their freedom."

</details>

**#260 only · main**

**#291 onward · main**

> Hraesvelgr refused peace, and Estinien means to kill Nidhogg in his lair, the Aery, which is walled behind impenetrable winds; he keeps watch until you are ready. In Ishgard you found Cid working on the Holy See's airship. The Enterprise can't dodge dragons, so Biggs and Wedge are finishing a small one, the manacutter. Then Tataru arrived with news of the sultana, and Cid sent you to Ul'dah.

Sources shown: Heart of Ice — main scenario quest (3.0); The Wyrm's Lair — main scenario quest (3.0); New Winds, Old Friends — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M290d** Nidhogg has walled the Aery behind impenetrable winds. *The Wyrm's Lair* (3.0, main): "You have at last discovered the Aery, but Nidhogg has surrounded his lair with a barrier of impenetrable winds."
  - **M291a** Estinien keeps watch on the Aery until you are ready to set out together. *New Winds, Old Friends* (3.0, main): "Contact me by linkpearl when your preparations are complete, and we shall set forth from Ishgard together."
  - **M291b** Cid is in Ishgard, working on the Holy See's ill-fated airship. *New Winds, Old Friends* (3.0, main): "the latest gossip surrounding Cid and the Holy See's ill-fated [[airship]]."
  - **M291c** The Enterprise is too big to dodge dragons. *New Winds, Old Friends* (3.0, main): "The Dravanians would fly rings around her."
  - **M291d** Biggs and Wedge show off a small airship, the manacutter. *New Winds, Old Friends* (3.0, main): "Biggs and [[Wedge]] proudly display their newest invention—a diminutive airship known as a “[[manacutter]].”"
  - **M291e** Tataru brings news of the sultana, and Cid sends you to Ul'dah while the manacutter is finished. *New Winds, Old Friends* (3.0, main): "The receptionist has news of the [[Nanamo Ul Namo|sultana]]! Noting the urgency of the situation, Cid bids you concentrate on matters in [[Ul'dah]] while he and his engineers continue work on the manacutter."

> A dragon of Anyx Trine and Ysayle's friend, without whose help the way to Sohm Al's summit stays closed. She will not leave her post while the Gnath's god threatens her kin, and resents that Estinien carries Nidhogg's stolen eye.

Sources shown: The Trine Towers — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M273a** Without the help of the dragons at Anyx Trine, the way to Sohm Al's summit stays closed. *The Trine Towers* (3.0, main): "Without their cooperation, she claims, the way to [[Sohm Al]]'s summit will remain closed."
  - **M273b** Vidofnir must stay to protect her kin from the Gnath's god. *The Trine Towers* (3.0, main): "I am bound to remain here, and protect my kin from the Gnath's god."
  - **M273d** Vidofnir knows Estinien carries Nidhogg's stolen eye. *The Trine Towers* (3.0, main): "when thine own companion beareth Nidhogg's stolen eye!?"
  - **M273e** Alphinaud offers to remove the threat in return for Vidofnir's help. *The Trine Towers* (3.0, main): "if we were to eliminate the threat to your territory, would you consent to Lady Ysayle's request?"

</details>

**#279–3.0 · main**

> A dragon of Anyx Trine and Ysayle's friend. With the Gnath's god defeated, she kept her word and opened the way through Mourn to Sohm Al's summit, warning Estinien to keep his stolen power in check.

Sources shown: The Trine Towers — main scenario quest (3.0); Mourn in Passing — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M273e** Alphinaud offers to remove the threat in return for Vidofnir's help. *The Trine Towers* (3.0, main): "if we were to eliminate the threat to your territory, would you consent to Lady Ysayle's request?"
  - **M279a** Vidofnir opens the way through Mourn to Sohm Al's summit. *Mourn in Passing* (3.0, main): "hie you unto the deepest reaches of Mourn, and there shall you find Halo─the altar from which you may begin your ascent to the summit of Sohm Al."
  - **M279d** Vidofnir warns Estinien to keep his stolen power in check. *Mourn in Passing* (3.0, main): "have care to keep the stolen power thou wieldest in check, lest it breed further despair."

</details>

**#336 only · main**

> A dragon of Hraesvelgr's brood at Anyx Trine, with whom Ser Aymeric has sent Lucia to treat.

Sources shown: An Uncertain Future — main scenario quest (3.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M336d** Aymeric sends you to escort Lucia to Anyx Trine to treat with Vidofnir and restore relations with Hraesvelgr's brood. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "Ser Aymeric bids you escort [[Lucia]] to [[Anyx Trine]], that she might treat with [[Vidofnir]] and thereby reestablish diplomatic relations with [[Hraesvelgr]]'s brood."

</details>

**#337–#340 · main**

> Hraesvelgr's daughter, at Anyx Trine. Lucia asked her for Ishgard's friendship, telling her that King Thordan betrayed and murdered Ratatoskr. She must consult her sire before answering, and will not leave her people while the Gnath grow bold.

Sources shown: Breaking the Cycle — main scenario quest (3.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M337a** Lucia tells Vidofnir that King Thordan and his knights betrayed and murdered Ratatoskr. *Breaking the Cycle* (3.1, main): "King Thordan and his knights twelve did willfully betray and murder the great wyrm Ratatoskr, shattering the peace between our peoples."
  - **M337c** Vidofnir must consult her sire before she answers. *Breaking the Cycle* (3.1, main): "This matter concerneth my sire. He must needs be consulted."
  - **M337d** Vidofnir says the Gnath grow bold again. *Breaking the Cycle* (3.1, main): "Moreover, the Gnath grow bold, even as they did before, and I would not leave my people at the mercy of the swarm."

</details>

**#341–#342 · main**

> Hraesvelgr's daughter, at Anyx Trine. She is glad that Ravana has fallen, and, her sire having left the choice to her, she will journey to Ishgard on behalf of her people.

Sources shown: Breaking the Cycle — main scenario quest (3.1); Dreams of the Lost — main scenario quest (3.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M337c** Vidofnir must consult her sire before she answers. *Breaking the Cycle* (3.1, main): "This matter concerneth my sire. He must needs be consulted."

  - **M341b** Hraesvelgr has mourned for a thousand years his beloved, who gave her life for a peace a king betrayed. *Dreams of the Lost* (3.1, main): "For a thousand years I have mourned my beloved, who gave her life to forge a peace thy king betrayed."
  - **M341c** Vidofnir will journey to Ishgard on behalf of her people. *Dreams of the Lost* (3.1, main): "Let it be known that I, Vidofnir, shall journey unto Ishgard on behalf of my people."

</details>

### Ravana (`char-ravana`, character)

**#278 onward · main** · Also searchable as: Master of the Sacred Blades, Wrath of the Colony

> The primal of the Gnath, Master of the Sacred Blades and Wrath of the Colony, given form by their prayers for the Dravanians' death. He defeated Ysayle as Saint Shiva, but you beat him, and he vowed to call his followers back from the dragons' domain.

Sources shown: Lord of the Hive — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M278a** Ravana, Master of the Sacred Blades and Wrath of the Colony, comes to claim his sacrifices. *Lord of the Hive* (3.0, main): "Lord [[Ravana]], Master of the Sacred Blades and Wrath of the Colony, arrives to claim his sacrifices."
  - **M278b** The Gnath's prayers for the Dravanians' death gave Ravana form. *Lord of the Hive* (3.0, main): "The Gnath would see the Dravanians slain, and their territory secured─and by such fervent prayers am I now given form and purpose."
  - **M278d** Ysayle draws on the Gnath's crystals to become Saint Shiva. *Lord of the Hive* (3.0, main): "Ysayle draws upon the energy of the Gnath's hoarded crystals to transform herself into Saint [[Shiva]], and battle is joined."
  - **M278e** Ravana, defeated, vows to call his followers back from the dragons' domain. *Lord of the Hive* (3.0, main): "vows to call his followers back from the dragons' domain."

</details>

### Ul'dah Set Right (`evt-uldah-set-right`, event)

**#292 only · main**

> The Scions were branded fugitives after the sultana's apparent poisoning at a royal banquet in Ul'dah. Raubahn has found she lies alive in a deathlike sleep. Yugiri traced her former lady-in-waiting, Meriel, but Lord Lolorito stepped in and confessed: he had Meriel give the sultana a sleeping potion instead of poison, and had Ilberd lie about the assassination to turn Raubahn's rage on Teledji. He handed over the means to wake her, and Raubahn was reinstated as Flame General.

Sources shown: The Parting Glass — main scenario quest (2.55); A General Summons — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C50** At the banquet the Scions are accused of conspiring to poison the sultana, detained, and branded fugitives. *The Parting Glass* (2.55, main): "I hereby accuse you of regicide! … all members of the Scions of the Seventh Dawn will be detained for questioning … branded fugitives"
  - **M292a** Raubahn believes the sultana lies alive, abed somewhere in the palace. *A General Summons* (3.0, main): "Her Grace is likely somewhere within the palace─abed but alive."
  - **M292b** Yugiri learns that Meriel, the sultana's former lady-in-waiting, is hiding in the Silver Bazaar. *A General Summons* (3.0, main): "the sultana's former lady-in-waiting, is hiding somewhere in the"
  - **M292c** Lolorito appears before Meriel can be questioned and reveals the assassination plot himself. *A General Summons* (3.0, main): "appears and proceeds to reveal the details of the assassination plot"

**#332 only · main**

> Cid's aetheric ram, powered by Nidhogg's Eye, broke Azys Lla's barrier, and you have followed the archbishop onto the isle. ### The Conference at Falcon's Nest (`evt-falcons-nest-conference`, event)

**#346 only · main**

There Lucia, once a foreign spy who pledged herself to Ishgard, oversees a relief to be unveiled. Alphinaud asks you to keep Minfilia's fate from the others.

  - **M346g** A relief at Falcon's Nest will be unveiled during the conference. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "It conceals a relief that will be unveiled during the conference."
